description:
Ranked #3 in docs/research/string-workloads.md (defk-dtw.20). Anchors: murmur (2.4M downloads, pure Elixir), xxhash (205k, pure Elixir, README: "consider creating a NIF of xxHash if you require a high performance version"), siphash (224k, 108-line hand-written C next to an Elixir fallback, README claims ~200x), crc32cer (48.5M, wraps Google's SIMD crc32c with a dirty twin), evil_crc32c (38.8k, 66 lines of hand-written Rust, bit-at-a-time), spirit_fingers (SimHash, ~200 lines of Rust).

Why a kernel and not :erlang.phash2 or :erlang.crc32: a specific hash must match other systems (Kafka, sharding, dedup indexes); phash2 is not portable across OTP versions and crc32 is one polynomial. Both BIFs are reported beside the verdict as the ceiling (measured in the research: phash2 2.6 GB/s, crc32 ~39 GB/s on 16 MiB).

Shape: [u8] plus a seed or 16-byte key in, i64 (u64 bits) or a 16-byte [u8] out. Realistic size: 16 B to a few MB; measure a batch of 1k short keys per call and one 4 MB message.

Design: one example file with xxHash64, Murmur3 x64_128 and SipHash-2-4 as kernels; CRC32C table-driven (the 256-entry table built in the kernel, works today) as a fourth. Agreement against the anchor packages' own outputs (their test vectors) and against Elixir mode. Elixir baselines: the murmur and xxhash packages themselves and siphash's fallback, marked :optimized after checking they use bitwise BIFs sensibly (they are the community's best pure versions).

Expected verdicts: good against murmur/xxhash/siphash-fallback (pure Elixir bignum and bitwise), marginal against siphash's C NIF, poor against crc32cer's SIMD (report, do not hide).

Needs: defk-w38 with masked arithmetic (CONTEXT.md "how hashes and checksums wrap"), defk-n4r.2 (u64_le(bytes, i), wrapping * and +, rotates), defk-ivt for the primes and seeds. u64 results: the kernel returns the i64 bit pattern; the example documents that Elixir callers reinterpret with `<<u::unsigned-64>> = <<h::signed-64>>` until a u64 scalar exists.

Done when: all four hashes pass their reference vectors, verdicts are measured and the README tables get the rows, with the NIF and BIF comparisons beside them.
title: Target workload: non-cryptographic hashes (xxHash64, Murmur3, SipHash, CRC32C) vs murmur, xxhash, siphash and crc32cer
